lessons.title: What is JavaScript?
lessons.description: What JavaScript does, how to add it to a page, and how to see its output and errors in the console.
hints: Open the console with F12 or Ctrl+Shift+J on Windows, or Cmd+Option+J on a Mac.
The preview re-runs your code every time it changes, so messages repeat in the console. Clear it (Ctrl+L) before checking your output.
JavaScript is case-sensitive: console.log works, but Console.log and console.Log do not.
Put the <script> element just before </body>, so the page has loaded before your code runs.

lessons.title: Variables and Data Types
lessons.description: Storing values in variables, the main types of data, and combining text and numbers.
hints: Use const by default, and let only for a value that needs to change. A const cannot be given a new value.
A string must start and end with the same kind of quote: 'text' or "text".
Template literals use backticks, not quotes, with values inside ${}, e.g. `Hello, ${name}!`
"5" + 5 gives "55", because + joins strings. Convert text to a number first with Number("5").

lessons.title: Operators and Conditionals
lessons.description: Comparing values and making decisions in your code with if statements.
hints: A single = assigns a value. To compare two values, use ===.
Always use === and !== rather than == and !=, which convert types first and can give surprising results.
&& means both conditions must be true; || means at least one must be true.
The condition goes in round brackets and the code to run goes in curly braces: if (score >= 50) { ... }

lessons.title: Functions
lessons.description: Grouping code into reusable functions that take inputs and return results.
hints: Defining a function does not run it. Call it by writing its name followed by brackets, e.g. greet();
return sends a value back to where the function was called, and stops the function immediately.
Variables declared inside a function only exist inside that function.
An arrow function is a shorter way to write a function, e.g. const add = (a, b) => a + b;

lessons.title: The DOM: Selecting and Changing Elements
lessons.description: Finding elements on the page with JavaScript and changing their text, classes and attributes.
hints: querySelector uses CSS selectors, so IDs need a # and classes need a full stop, e.g. document.querySelector('#title').
If querySelector returns null, no element matched. Check the selector's spelling against the HTML.
querySelectorAll returns a list of elements, so you need a loop to change each one.
Use textContent to change text. Never put user input into innerHTML, as it can run harmful code.

lessons.title: Events
lessons.description: Making the page respond to clicks, typing and key presses.
hints: Pass the function itself, without brackets: button.addEventListener('click', handleClick); Writing handleClick() runs it straight away instead.
Event names are lowercase, with no "on" at the start: 'click', not 'onClick'.
Inside the event handler, event.target is the element that the event happened on.
The 'input' event fires every time the value of a text box changes, so it is ideal for live updates.

lessons.title: Arrays and Loops
lessons.description: Storing lists of values in arrays, and repeating code for each item with loops and array methods.
hints: Array indexes start at 0, so the first item is items[0] and the last is items[items.length - 1].
If a loop never ends, the platform stops it after a second. Check that the loop's condition will eventually become false.
map returns a new array with every item changed; filter returns a new array of only the matching items.
find returns the first matching item, or undefined if nothing matches. forEach returns nothing at all.

lessons.title: Objects
lessons.description: Grouping related data into objects, and working with arrays of objects.
hints: Properties are written as name: value, separated by commas, e.g. { title: 'HTML Basics', level: 'beginner' }
Use dot notation (session.title) for known property names, and brackets (session[key]) when the name is in a variable.
Reading a property that does not exist gives undefined. If a value is missing, check the property name's spelling.
In an array of objects, loop through the array, then use dot notation on each object.

lessons.title: Creating Elements From Data
lessons.description: Building page content from data, and updating it when the data changes.
hints: createElement makes a new element, but it does not appear on the page until you add it with append.
Put data onto the page with textContent, not innerHTML, so it is always treated as text.
Before re-rendering a list, clear the old items first with container.replaceChildren();
For elements created later, add one listener to their parent, and use event.target.closest() to find which one was clicked.

lessons.title: Interactive Components
lessons.description: Building accordions, tabs and live filters, and keeping them accessible.
hints: Store the current state in a variable, such as which tab is open, and update the page from that variable.
Use JavaScript to add and remove classes, and let CSS decide how each class looks.
aria-expanded must be updated every time a section opens or closes, using setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true').
For a search that ignores capitals, convert both the search text and the item text with toLowerCase() before comparing.

lessons.title: JavaScript and Responsive Design
lessons.description: Building a mobile navigation menu, responding to media queries in JavaScript, and respecting user preferences.
hints: Let CSS show or hide the menu button at each screen size. JavaScript should only toggle a class.
Update the menu button's aria-expanded every time the menu opens or closes.
window.matchMedia('(min-width: 600px)').matches is true when the preview is at least 600px wide.
Test the mobile menu in a narrow pop-out preview, as in the CSS unit.

lessons.title: Consolidation: Build an Interactive Page
lessons.description: Build an interactive session browser for the Beginners' Web Workshop, using everything from this unit.
hints: Build one feature at a time, and check it works before starting the next.
Use console.log to check your data at each step, e.g. console.log(filteredSessions);
If a feature stops working, undo your last change and check it works again, then make the change in smaller steps.
Test the page in both a narrow pop-out preview and the fullscreen preview.
